symbols.name: place count
symbols.meaning: The number of places in the mixed-radix system.
symbols.quote: Fix a positive integer $\beta$, the number of places, and positive integers $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_\beta$.

symbols.name: place index
symbols.meaning: The index of a place, running from 1 to beta.
symbols.quote: The place index $j$ runs from $1$ to $\beta$ and names a place.

symbols.name: place length
symbols.meaning: The number of values the digit at place j can take.
symbols.quote: Here $\lambda_j$ is the length of place $j$, the number of values the digit at place $j$ can take.

symbols.name: total length
symbols.meaning: The product of all place lengths, which counts the distinct digit strings the system can write.
symbols.quote: Let $\Lambda = \lambda_1\lambda_2\cdots\lambda_\beta$ be the product of the lengths, the number of distinct digit strings the system can write.

symbols.name: place value
symbols.meaning: The product of the lengths of the places below place j, so that one unit of the digit at place j adds w_j to the integer.
symbols.quote: The place value of place $j$ is $w_j = \lambda_1\lambda_2\cdots\lambda_{j-1}$, the product of the lengths of the places below it, with $w_1 = 1$.

symbols.name: integer being written
symbols.meaning: The nonnegative integer, less than Lambda, whose mixed-radix expansion is taken.
symbols.quote: Let $\nu$ be an integer with $0 \le \nu < \Lambda$, the integer being written.

symbols.name: digit at place j
symbols.meaning: The digit of an expansion at place j, an integer from 0 up to lambda_j minus 1.
symbols.quote: The digit $v_j$ at place $j$ is an integer with $0 \le v_j < \lambda_j$.

symbols.name: common length
symbols.meaning: The common length of every place in a uniform system, which counts the digit values 0 through rho minus 1.
symbols.quote: If every length equals a common value $\rho$, the number of digit values $0,\dots,\rho-1$, the expansion is the base-$\rho$ expansion.

symbols.name: dummy place index
symbols.meaning: A place index running over the places below j in sums.
symbols.quote: Here $i$ is a place index that runs over the places below $j$, so the letter changes meaning from its use on the convolution page.

relations.quote: Uniqueness of the expansion is based on the [Telescoping identity](telescoping-identity.md).
